Unit 11 • SL

Global Networking

Introduction

How does the world stay connected?

This unit focuses on Interconnectivity and Standardisation. You will explore how heterogeneous systems communicate through common rules (Protocols) and the physical architecture required to move data globally, from local LANs to the massive WAN of the Internet.

You'll begin by defining network types (LAN, WAN, VPN) and hardware (Routers, Switches). Then you'll map out Topologies and model data flow using Packet Switching and TCP/IP. Finally, you'll secure these networks using Encryption and Firewalls.

Network Fundamentals

Networks are defined by scale and architecture:

  • LAN (Local): Small area, high speed (e.g., Home/School).
  • WAN (Wide): Large area, connects LANs (e.g., The Internet).
  • VPN (Virtual Private): A secure tunnel over a public WAN.

Packet Switching

Data doesn't travel in one big chunk. It is broken into Packets.

  • Breakdown: File sliced into packets.
  • Routing: Each packet takes the fastest route (independent paths).
  • Reassembly: Packets reordered at the destination.

Protocols (The Rules)

Computers must agree on how to talk. We use standard protocols:

  • TCP/IP: The fundamental language of the internet.
  • HTTP/HTTPS: Web pages (Secure vs plain).
  • DHCP: Assigning IP addresses automatically.

Security & Encryption

The internet is public. To keep secrets, we use math.

  • Firewall: A filter that checks incoming/outgoing packets.
  • Symmetric Encryption: Same key to lock and unlock (Fast, but how to share key?).
  • Asymmetric Encryption: Public key to lock, Private key to unlock (Secure key exchange).

Key Terminology
TermDefinition
ProtocolA set of rules defining how two computers communicate (e.g., format, speed, error checking).
BandwidthThe theoretical maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over a connection in a given time.
LatencyThe time delay between the request for data and the receipt of the data.
Packet SwitchingMethod of slicing data into packets, routing them individually, and reassembling them at the destination.
RouterA device that forwards data packets between computer networks (typically joining a LAN to a WAN).
SwitchA device that connects devices within a LAN and uses MAC addresses to filter traffic.
EncryptionEncoding data so that only authorized parties can understand it.
VPNVirtual Private Network. Extends a private network across a public network allowing secure data exchange.
TopologyThe physical or logical arrangement of a network (e.g., Star, Mesh, Bus).

Common Misconceptions

Web vs Internet

Thinking they are the same. The Internet is the infrastructure (Roads). The Web is just one service on it (Traffic).

WiFi = Internet

Assuming a WiFi signal means you have Internet. You can have strong WiFi (LAN) but no connection to the ISP (WAN).

Switch vs Router

Thinking they do the same job. Switches create a network (LAN). Routers connect networks (LAN to WAN).

Think Deeper

"The Digital Divide" If access to the internet defines access to knowledge and opportunity, is internet access a human right? Does the physical infrastructure dictate who can succeed?
